content.title: LinkedIn — what buyers miss on light jet value
content.hook: The cheapest light jet on the market is almost never the best buy.
content.body:
The cheapest light jet on the market is almost never the best buy.

Asking price is the number everyone looks at. It's also the number that tells you the least. What actually moves your total cost of ownership is the stuff a spec sheet buries:

— Are the engines on a program, or are you one hot section away from a six-figure surprise?
— When was the last major inspection, and how much runway is left before the next one?
— Is the avionics stack current enough to fly the airspace you actually fly?

We've watched buyers save a hundred grand on acquisition and give it all back in the first year. Position beats price. Know what you're really buying before you're asked to defend it.

content.title: LinkedIn — fresh maintenance is repricing the market
content.hook: Fresh maintenance is quietly repricing the used-jet market.
content.body:
Fresh maintenance is quietly repricing the used-jet market.

For years, buyers chased the lowest sticker. That's changing. With shop slots backed up and inspection costs climbing, a jet that's already had its big-ticket work done — fresh inspections, engines on a program — is trading at a real premium and selling faster.

The reason is simple: the next owner isn't buying an airplane, they're buying a position. A clean, current maintenance outlook means predictable costs and no six-figure surprise in year one.

If you're weighing two similar jets, look past the asking price to what's already been paid for. That gap is where the value hides.

content.title: Why a Fresh Pre-Buy Protects a Buyer's Position
content.hook: A pre-buy inspection isn't a formality. It's leverage.
content.body:
Most negotiating power in an aircraft transaction shifts the moment the pre-buy findings come back. A thorough, independent inspection gives a buyer an accurate picture of the aircraft's true condition — not the seller's version of it, not the logbook summary, the actual state of the airframe, engines, and systems.

That picture is what lets you negotiate from fact instead of assumption. Discrepancies found during a pre-buy aren't obstacles — they're information. They tell you what to fix, what to price in, and what to walk away from.

Skipping or shortcutting this step to move faster almost always costs more later, in unplanned maintenance, in resale value, or in disputes that could have been settled before closing.

Know the aircraft's condition before you're asked to defend your offer — or your exit.

content.title: Facebook — the value is in the cabin (concept)
content.hook: Most people picture a private jet from the outside. The difference is on the inside.
content.body:
It's easy to judge an aircraft by the ramp shot. But the part that changes your day is the cabin — the four hours you actually spend in it.

A true stand-up cabin means you're not folding yourself into a seat. A quiet cabin means a real conversation, or a call that doesn't fall apart. Room to spread out means you can work, eat, or sleep without negotiating for the space.

Here's the honest part: cabins vary enormously between models. The right aircraft depends on how far you fly, how many people travel with you, and what you need to get done onboard. That's the conversation we have with every client — before anyone talks about a specific airplane.

Tell us how you fly and we'll help you find the fit.
